name: Travel Markers (Auto Travel)
summary: Allows you to set points of interest (Bases, towns, anything really) and select your characters then select the saved point and they will automatically go there without needing to go to the map screen.
description:
[b][size=6]Travel Markers[/size][/b]

[b][color=#ff0000]REQUIRES RE_Kenshi 0.3.5 or newer. Without RE_Kenshi this mod does nothing.[/color][/b]

Travel Markers lets you save named travel markers (bases, cities, points of interest, danger zones) at any character's position, then send a whole squad there with one click.

[b]FEATURES[/b]
[list]
[*]Add a marker at the selected character's position, name it, and give it a type: Base, City, POI or Danger.[/*]
[*][b]Go[/b] sends the selected characters to the marker in a loose formation. [b]Home[/b] sends them to your first Base marker.[/*]
[*]Tick [b]Run[/b] to run instead of jog. Each member's previous walk/jog/run setting is put back when the group arrives or halts.[/*]
[*]Arrival message when the group gets there, and a warning if somebody is still far away a minute later.[/*]
[*][b]Contact![/b] warning when a member is attacked, in combat, or a hostile character is close. Optional [b]auto-stop on contact[/b], then [b]Resume[/b] when you are ready.[/*]
[*][b]Focus[/b] jumps the camera to the group. Clicking a Contact message does the same.[/*]
[*]Markers belong to your [b]campaign[/b], not to one save file: they follow you across quicksaves, autosaves and named saves, and stay separate for different playthroughs. A Campaign panel lets you rename, split or merge campaigns if the automatic match ever guesses wrong.[/*]
[*]Delete, Detach and Link ask for a second click so nothing disappears by accident.[/*]
[*][b]Cancel trip[/b] ends a trip without giving any orders.[/*]
[*]Export and import markers to back them up or share them.[/*]
[/list]
[b]REQUIREMENTS[/b]
[list]
[*][b]RE_Kenshi 0.3.5 or newer[/b][/*]
[*]Tested on Kenshi 1.0.68 (Steam) with RE_Kenshi 0.3.5. GOG and 1.0.65 should work but are untested.[/*]
[/list]
[b]INSTALLATION[/b]

[list=1]
[*]Extract the TravelMarkers folder into your Kenshi mods folder, so that [i]<Kenshi>\mods\TravelMarkers\TravelMarkers.dll[/i] exists.[/*]
[*]Install RE_Kenshi and start Kenshi through it.[/*]
[*]Tick TravelMarkers in the launcher's Mods tab.[/*]
[*]Load a game. A Markers button appears near the right edge of the screen, or press F8.[/*]
[/list]
To uninstall, untick the mod and delete the folder. Your markers live in its [i]data[/i] folder, so back that up first if you want to keep them.

[b]CONTROLS[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Markers button / F8[/b]: show or hide the window[/*]
[*][b]Add at selected / Rename / Delete[/b]: manage markers (Delete needs a second click)[/*]
[*][b]Go / Home[/b]: send the selected characters to the chosen marker / to your Base[/*]
[*][b]Run[/b]: run instead of jog during the trip[/*]
[*][b]Auto-stop on contact[/b]: halt the group when enemies show up[/*]
[*][b]Focus / Resume[/b]: camera to the group / continue after an auto-stop[/*]
[*][b]Cancel trip[/b]: end the trip; characters keep doing what they are doing[/*]
[*][b]Export / Import[/b]: back up or share markers[/*]
[*][b]Campaign...[/b]: rename, split (detach) or merge (link) campaigns[/*]
[/list]Settings live in [i]TravelMarkers.ini[/i] next to the DLL (hotkey, button position, detection radius and so on).

[b]KNOWN LIMITATIONS[/b]
[list]
[*]After loading a save, Go and Add are disabled for a few seconds while your squads finish loading ("Campaign: loading..."). This is on purpose.[/*]
[*]Campaigns are recognised by the characters on your team. If you start a new game with the same starting characters as an old one, or swap your whole team, you may need to use Detach or Link once.[/*]
[*]Orders are sent once. If the game's AI cancels a move order on its own (for example in a fight), press Go or Resume again.[/*]
[*]Travel timers use real time and keep running while the game is paused.[/*]
[*]Contact detection may also react to hostile animals or distant hostile factions inside the detection radius. Lower [i]contactRadius[/i] or set [i]nearbyScan=0[/i] in the ini if it is too jumpy.[/*]
[*]Distances (arrival radius, formation spread, contact radius) are tuned by feel; adjust them in the ini if members never count as arrived.[/*]
[*]No clicking on the map to place markers, no minimap overlay, no multi-stop routes.[/*]
[/list]
[b]COMPATIBILITY[/b]

It does not change game data or saves; it only adds a window and sends normal move orders. It should work alongside other mods, but mods that rebuild the whole GUI or change how characters are stored may affect the window or campaign matching. If characters do not move when you press Go, set [i]moveMethod=2[/i] or [i]3[/i] in the ini and restart.

[b]SOURCE AND LICENCE[/b]

The full source code for this version is uploaded on this page as the optional file TravelMarkers-1.0.2-source.zip. Licensed under the GNU General Public License v3 (GPLv3), like KenshiLib, which this mod is built on. See LICENSE in the download.

name: TimeLight Map - In-Game 3D Map
summary: A live 3D map in a corner of your screen that follows your squad. Every man shows as a labeled mark, and a dotted cone shows where your camera is looking. Set the corner, size, zoom and follow, or turn it off. Needs MeitouClient.
description:
[size=5][b]TimeLight Map[/b][/size]
A live 3D map in a corner of your screen that follows your squad. It isn't a drawn map: it's the game world itself, rendered a second time from above.

[size=4][b]What it shows[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Your people as dots with their names (the first member in gold, selected ones ringed, a hollow dot for anyone out cold, a small arrow on anyone walking)[/*]
[*]Hostile characters as red dots[/*]
[*]The names of towns and places you have discovered[/*]
[*]A dotted cone showing where your camera is and which way it looks[/*]
[*]A scale bar and a north arrow[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]What you can set[/b][/size]
In a small config file, or live in the game's console with the [b]topcam[/b] command:
[list]
[*]Corner: top-left, top-right, bottom-left or bottom-right[/*]
[*]Size and margin[/*]
[*]Zoom (10 m to 5 km across) and follow (your squad, your camera, or stay put)[/*]
[*]Tilt and see-through[/*]
[*]Each kind of mark on or off: names, red dots, towns, cone, arrows, scale bar, north arrow[/*]
[*]The whole map on or off[/*]
[/list]Every key and command is listed in README.txt inside the download.

[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][url=https://github.com/VlcekM/MeitouClient]MeitouClient[/url] 0.19.x (TimeLight Map 1.1.0). On MeitouClient 0.17.x, use 1.0.0 from the old files. It does [b]not[/b] work on stock Kenshi or RE_Kenshi.[/*]
[*]Developed and tested on MeitouClient's Linux (Vulkan) build. The Windows build is untried, so please tell us in the comments if it works for you.[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Install[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Copy the [b]TimeLightMap[/b] folder from the zip into the [b]mods[/b] folder of your Kenshi install.[/*]
[*]Start the MeitouClient launcher and make sure TimeLightMap is ticked.[/*]
[*]Load a save: the map is in the top-right corner, following your squad.[/*]
[/list]Optional: copy timelight-map.cfg.sample to mods/TimeLightMap/timelight-map.cfg and edit it to change the defaults.
To remove it, untick it or delete the folder. It keeps nothing in your saves.

[size=4][b]Good to know[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]The DLL is called Meitou.Tests.dll on purpose. MeitouClient keeps its renderer internal and lets exactly one assembly name see it. It's this mod's own code (the full source is included), and it ties each build to one MeitouClient line: 1.1.0 runs on 0.19.x, 1.0.0 on 0.17.x. A later MeitouClient release may need a new build.[/*]
[*]The map is a second render of the scene, so it costs some frame time. If your fps drops, try topcam size small, topcam scale 0.5 or topcam fps 15.[/*]
[*]Red dots show every character the game counts as hostile, whether your people can see them or not. Turn them off with topcam hostiles off.[/*]
[*]Running the Faction Caravans mod on MeitouClient? You may see small coloured squares on its pack bulls. They come from that mod's data on MeitouClient, not from this map, and show with or without it.[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]License[/b][/size]
GPL-3.0-or-later. The full source is the optional "source" file on this page, and it's also on [url=https://github.com/pizzy00/timelight-map]GitHub[/url]. Also on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3839458940]Steam Workshop[/url]. Uses Harmony (MIT), which ships with MeitouClient. No game files are included.

[size=4][b]About[/b][/size]
Built by the Kenshi Live Show team for our own Kenshi project. This is the first piece we're releasing as a standalone mod, and more are coming. Feedback and feature requests are welcome in the comments.

Kenshi Live Show, our stream where a local AI plays Kenshi by itself 24/7: [url=https://twitch.tv/beepistoostrong]twitch.tv/beepistoostrong[/url]

A new Heavy class weapon: a Greatsword.

[b]Location[/b]
The weapon and blueprint can be found at Catun, The Holy Nation, Mongrel, Ronin Vendors, the Scraphouse, the Shek Kingdom, and the United Cities. The Great Library in Black Scratch should also be guaranteed to have the blueprint.

Vs. Robots: [b]1.0[/b]

Indoors Modifier: [b]-6[/b]
Value: [b]525[/b]

You can also find this mod on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3814216043]Steam Workshop[/url]

name: Kenshi AddItemMenu
summary: Browse items from Kenshi and loaded mods, search by name, choose quality, and spawn them for your selected character.
description:
[size=6][b]Kenshi AddItemMenu[/b][/size]
Find items from Kenshi and your loaded mods, choose their quality, and add them to your character in game.

[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
Kenshi AddItemMenu adds an in-game item catalog. Press Ctrl+F10, choose Kenshi or a loaded mod, find an item, and click its entry. Each click gives you one copy of that exact variant.

Useful for testing mods, setting up scenes, trying equipment, and sandbox play. Items are free: no purchase or crafting required.

[size=4][b]Features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Browse base-game and loaded-mod items in one window. Kenshi items have categories; other mods open directly to their item lists.[/*]
[*]Case-insensitive name search, including Russian text and equivalent е/ё matching.[/*]
[*]Choose melee weapon manufacturer and quality model from the loaded database, including Meitou when its record is available.[/*]
[*]Six quality grades for armour, clothing, crossbows, and prosthetic limbs, from Prototype to Masterwork. Armour material variants are available where defined.[/*]
[*]Backpacks, food, medical supplies, ammunition, general items, maps, and blueprints. Consumables start fully charged.[/*]
[*]Items go to your selected player character. When inventory space is insufficient, they drop beside the character.[/*]
[*]English and Russian interface: Russian for a Russian game locale, English for all other locales. Existing window captions update when the locale changes. Item names come from the game database and installed translations.[/*]
[*]Configurable hotkey, optional Items button, and detailed logging through ModConfigMenu.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Kenshi x64 with a supported Steam or GOG 1.0.65 executable. Other executable versions are not supported by this release.[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/kenshi/mods/847]RE_Kenshi[/url] and a compatible KenshiLib.[/*]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/kenshi/mods/2202]ModConfigMenu[/url] for changing the hotkey and other settings in game. The default Ctrl+F10 shortcut works without it. Do not install a duplicate MCM if your setup already includes one.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Installation[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install RE_Kenshi with the required KenshiLib.[/*]
[*]Extract the archive into your Kenshi game directory. The plugin should be at Kenshi/mods/Kenshi AddItemMenu/plugin/KenshiAddItemMenu.dll.[/*]
[*]Enable Kenshi AddItemMenu in the launcher's mod list.[/*]
[*]Launch with RE_Kenshi active and load a save. A save import is not required to use the catalog.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]How to use[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Select one of your characters and press Ctrl+F10.[/*]
[*]Choose a source: Kenshi → category → items; another mod → items.[/*]
[*]Type part of an item's name in Search on the final item list.[/*]
[*]Click the desired quality entry. Click again for additional copies.[/*]
[/list]Back returns to the previous page. Escape or the close button closes the window. Refresh rebuilds the catalog from the current game database. The first opening may take a while with a large mod setup.

Settings are available under MCM → Kenshi AddItemMenu. The optional Items button is disabled by default.

[size=4][b]Compatibility and limitations[/b][/size]
The catalog uses the running game's final records, respecting load order. An item can appear under several mods if they define or override it; each list gives the same final version.

The plugin does not create duplicate FCS records or rewrite source item stats or recipes. Spawned items are saved normally and retain the dependencies of their original item mods.

Restart the game after enabling or disabling other mods. Refresh does not hot-load mods. Only supported inventory types are listed; internal, empty, and invalid records are filtered out. Custom item types introduced by third-party DLLs may need additional support. Compatibility with every mod setup is not guaranteed.

[size=4][b]Uninstalling and support[/b][/size]
Disable Kenshi AddItemMenu in the launcher and remove its folder. Spawned items remain normal game items; keep their original item mods installed if you want to retain them.

For bug reports, include KenshiAddItemMenu.log from the mod folder, the end of RE_Kenshi_log.txt, your executable version, and the item name and quality variant.
